Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/.claude/skills/markdown

# GitHub Flavored Markdown Generation

**Version:** 1.2.1

Generate GFM that passes markdownlint validation with zero violations.

## Core Principles

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

- Before/after ALL lists (MD032)
- Before/after ALL headings except document start (MD022)
- Before/after ALL code blocks (MD031)
- Between ALL block-level elements

### 2. Consistency Required

- Use `-` for lists
- Use `#` for headings (ATX)
- Regular spaces only—never tabs/nbsp

### 3. Structure Matters

- Heading hierarchy: 1→2→3 (not 1→3)
- ONE H1 per document
- Files end with one newline
- Lines under 80 chars

### 4. Invisible Characters Matter

- Use ONLY regular spaces (U+0020)
- Never non-breaking spaces (U+00A0,  )
- Never tabs
- UTF-8 encoding

## Pre-Generation Checklist

- [ ] Where will lists/headings/code appear?
- [ ] Heading levels verified (1→2→3)?
- [ ] Using `-` for all lists?
- [ ] Code languages specified?
- [ ] Lines under 80 chars?
- [ ] Line breaks needed? (two trailing spaces)
- [ ] Using regular spaces only?
- [ ] URLs wrapped in `<>` or `[]`?
- [ ] Document starts with H1?
- [ ] Ordered lists use `1.` for all items?
- [ ] File ends with single newline?
- [ ] Tables use consistent spacing?

## Essential Rules

### Lists (MD032, MD004)

```markdown
Text before.

- Item one
- Item two

Text after.
```

### Headings (MD001, MD022)

```markdown
Text.

## Heading

Content.
```

### Code Blocks (MD031, MD040)

````markdown
Text.

```python
code()
```

Text.
````

**Nested Fences:** When showing markdown examples that contain code blocks,
use **one more backtick** than the deepest level:

- Three backticks (` ``` `): Regular code
- Four backticks (` ```` `): Markdown examples with code
- Five backticks (` ````` `): Nested markdown examples

`````markdown
````markdown
# Example

```bash
command
```

````
`````

### Line Length (MD013)

Break long lines at natural points. Use reference-style links for long URLs.

### URLs and Email (MD034)

Wrap bare URLs and emails:

```markdown
Wrong: https://example.com
Right: <https://example.com>
Right: [link](https://example.com)

Wrong: user@example.com
Right: <user@example.com>
```

### Document Structure (MD041)

Start with H1 (or front matter then H1):

```markdown
# Document Title

First paragraph.
```

### Ordered Lists (MD029)

Use `1.` for all items:

```markdown
1. First
1. Second
1. Third
```

### File Endings (MD047)

End with single newline:

```text
Last content line.
[single newline]
[EOF]
```

### Table Column Style (MD060)

Use consistent spacing in tables. Three styles:

**Compact (recommended):** `| cell |` - single space around content

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Data | More data |
```

**Aligned:** Pipes vertically aligned with padding

**Tight:** `|cell|` - no spaces

Pick ONE style per document. Compact is preferred.

### Character Encoding

**Detection:** View → Render Whitespace in VS Code

**Fix:** Find `\u00A0` → Replace with space

**Critical for AI:** Two trailing spaces = intentional line breaks. Do NOT
remove them.

## Critical Error Patterns

### 1. List Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD032 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text:
- Item
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD032 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text:

- Item

Text.
```

### 2. Heading Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD022 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text.
## Head
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD022 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text.

## Head

Text.
```

### 3. Code Without Blanks/Language

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD031 MD040 -->

**Wrong:**

````markdown
Text:
```
code
```
Text.
````

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD031 MD040 -->

**Right:**

````markdown
Text:

```python
code
```

Text.
````

### 4. Inconsistent Markers

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
- Item
* Item
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD004 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
- Item
- Item
```

### 5. Skipping Levels

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
# Title

### Sub (skipped H2)
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
# Title

## Section

### Sub
```

## Post-Generation Validation

1. Lists have blank lines before/after
2. Headings have blank lines before/after
3. Code has blank lines before/after
4. Heading progression: 1→2→3→4
5. All lists use `-`
6. All code has language
7. Lines under 80 chars
8. Document starts with H1
9. URLs wrapped properly
10. Ordered lists use `1.`
11. File ends with one newline
12. Two trailing spaces used intentionally
13. Only regular spaces (no nbsp/tabs)
14. Tables use consistent column spacing

## Mental Model

Markdown is **blocks with mandatory spacing:**

```text
[Text Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Heading Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[List Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Code Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Text Block]
[EOF]
```

Every block transition = blank line required.

## Quick Patterns

**List:**

```markdown
text

- item

text
```

**Heading:**

```markdown
text

## Head

text
```

**Code:**

````markdown
text

```lang
code
```

text
````

**Nested:**

```markdown
- parent
  - child
- parent
```

**Ordered:**

```markdown
text

1. item
1. item

text
```

**Table:**

```markdown
text

| Header | Header |
| --- | --- |
| Cell | Cell |

text
```

## Common Languages

**Programming:** `python` `javascript` `java` `c` `cpp` `go` `rust` `ruby`
`php` `swift` `kotlin` `typescript`

**Shell:** `bash` `sh` `powershell` `cmd` `zsh`

**Markup:** `html` `css` `xml` `json` `yaml` `toml` `markdown`

**Database:** `sql` `postgresql` `mysql`

**Other:** `text` `diff` `log`

## Validation

```bash
markdownlint filename.md
```

Goal: Zero errors/warnings.

## Additional Resources

See bundled references:

- `references/complete-rules.md` - Full rule catalog
- `references/edge-cases.md` - Platform quirks
- `references/examples.md` - Detailed examples

## Remember

Most common: Missing blank lines around lists/headings/code.

**Two trailing spaces:** Intentional line breaks. Do NOT remove.

1. Add blank lines before/after blocks
2. Use `-` for lists
3. Use `#` for headings

/* Builds the unmodified galaxy.c in single precision (about 150 ms a frame in
 * double, 40 ms in float). */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "xlockmore.h"

#include "hacks/single_precision.h"

#include "galaxy/galaxy.c"
"""PlatformIO pre-build script: writes the copies of hacks with their decimal
literals made floats that src/hacks/*_single.c include. See
tools/float_literals.py for why."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
sys.path.insert(0, str(project.parent / "tools"))
import binaryring_patch
import celtic_patch
import etruscanvenus_patch
import fireworkx_patch
import float_literals

generated = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated"  # noqa: F821
generated.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

for name in ("braid",) + (
    "euler2d",
    "compass",
    "fuzzyflakes",
    "halftone",
    "interaggregate",
    "anemone",
    "lmorph",
    "hexadrop",
    "fireworkx",
    "starfish",
    "goop",
    "cwaves",
    "hextrail",
    "celtic",
    "binaryring",
    "piecewise",
    "etruscanvenus",
):
    source = (project / "src" / "hacks" / name / f"{name}.c").read_text()
    if name == "fireworkx":
        source = fireworkx_patch.scale_for_a_small_window(source)
    if name == "celtic":
        source = celtic_patch.compute_spline_position_once(source)
        source = celtic_patch.fit_the_graph_to_the_screen(source)
        source = celtic_patch.scale_the_animation_step(source)
    if name == "etruscanvenus":
        source = etruscanvenus_patch.size_the_grid(source)
    if name == "binaryring":
        source = binaryring_patch.float_random_scale(source)
    patched = float_literals.float_literals(source)
    target = generated / f"{name}_floatlit.c"
    if not target.exists() or target.read_text() != patched:
        target.write_text(patched)

env.Append(CPPPATH=[str(generated)])  # noqa: F821
17: * galaxy. -3 caps it at 3. Counts of -2 or above skip the hack's cleanup on
48:XLOCKMORE_HACK_WITH(galaxy, "Galaxy", kGalaxyOverrides);
209:    &galaxy_hack,

content.text:
Eight of the ten hacks are ported and running on the board. The other two (Rocks and DecayScreen) were wired in, looked at and dropped, so Triangle and XRaySwarm took their places. The work is on `feature/batch5-s-m-hacks` in a worktree: three commits, no push and no PR yet.

The full host suite passes (694 tests), as do the tools pytest (531 passed, 1 skipped), the notices check and markdownlint. The board is now on the normal rotating build, flashed and hash-verified.

## Ported

I read the fps figures from the second 5 s window on, over 45 s each. Nothing crashed or reset.

| Hack | fps | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Abstractile | 20.6–32.2 | Holds about 6.1 MB of PSRAM while running |
| Attraction | 59 | |
| Greynetic | 75–76 | |
| Wander | 37.6 | |
| PopSquares | 22.6 | |
| Lisa | 14.3 | 9.6 fps as copied, so it uses a single-precision wrapper (`lisa_single.c`) |
| Penrose | 77–90 | |
| Worm | 51.6 | |
| Triangle | 57–67 | Needed a wrapper (`triangle_colors.c`) so `colors.h` is included first |
| XRaySwarm | 22.8–23 | Needed a wrapper (`xrayswarm_time.c`) to turn on `gettimeofday` |

I added `XClearArea`, `XMaxRequestSize` and the dashed line-style constants to the shim, each with a test. Of the mutation checks, one mutant survived and is equivalent, because `canvas_fill_rect` already ignores a negative size.

## Dropped

- **Rocks:** it draws its big rocks into depth-1 pixmaps, which the shim leaves blank. Only tiny far dots appear.
- **DecayScreen:** it smears a grabbed screen image, and the shim grabs nothing, so it stays black.

Both are in `tools/failed_ports.txt`.

## What I haven't verified

- **Colour and look on the screen:** only you can say. Worm's worms are 1 px wide and there are only a few of them. XRaySwarm is white on the host, and I don't know whether that's its default look or a colour gap in the shim.
- **Rotation soak:** I skipped it. Five laps at 5 s each across the whole registry would take over three hours. Abstractile's PSRAM use is the thing to watch in one.
- **Speed predictions:** I didn't add the new hacks to the speed-backtest holdout.

## Your call

Triangle's wrapper exists because adding `colors.h` to the shim's shared `screenhackI.h` would change what every xlockmore hack sees. That would be a one-line include if you want it instead.

Next I'd push and open a draft PR with `entire trail create`, with the unverified items above in the body. Say if you want that, or if you'd rather look at the board first.

/* Shim replacement for xscreensaver's utils/ximage-loader.h. Not derived from
 * xscreensaver code.
 *
 * Upstream decodes a PNG. The device has no decoder, so the "image data" here
 * is a raw blob made on the Mac by tools/make_logo_blob.py:
 *
 *   bytes 0-3          the characters "565M"
 *   bytes 4-5          width, unsigned 16-bit little-endian
 *   bytes 6-7          height, unsigned 16-bit little-endian
 *   next width*height  pixels, row by row, each RGB565 as 16-bit little-endian
 *   remainder          mask, row by row, each row padded to whole bytes,
 *                      most significant bit first; 1 = draw the pixel
 *
 * The blob size must match its width and height exactly. */
#ifndef XSHIM_XIMAGE_LOADER_H
#define XSHIM_XIMAGE_LOADER_H

#include "x11shim/xshim.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* Returns a colour pixmap, and writes its size and a depth-1 mask pixmap
 * through the pointers. Returns None (and writes zeros and None) when the
 * blob is not valid or memory runs out. The caller frees both pixmaps. Any of
 * the three pointers may be NULL (xmatrix passes no mask, and none is made). */
Pixmap image_data_to_pixmap(Display *, Window, const unsigned char *data,
                            unsigned long size, int *width_ret,
                            int *height_ret, Pixmap *mask_ret);

/* The image as a 32-bit XImage of RGBA bytes (alpha 255 where the mask is set,
 * 0 where not), upside down, row 0 being the bottom, as upstream gives it for
 * glTexImage2D. NULL for a bad blob or no memory; free it with XDestroyImage. */
XImage *image_data_to_ximage(Display *, Visual *, const unsigned char *data,
                             unsigned long size);

/* Upstream reads an image file. The device has no filesystem for hacks and no
 * decoder, so this always returns NULL, and a hack that loads an optional
 * picture carries on without one. */
XImage *file_to_ximage(Display *, Visual *, const char *filename);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

"""Turn an image into the C header that Maze's logo is read from.

The device has no PNG decoder, so the image goes in as a raw RGB565 blob with
a 1-bit mask. The layout is documented in
firmware/src/x11shim/include/ximage-loader.h.

Run with: uv run tools/make_logo_blob.py logo-50.gif --name logo_50_png \\
    -o firmware/src/x11shim/include/images/gen/logo-50_png.h
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OPAQUE_ALPHA = 128


def rgb565(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> int:
    return (r & 0xF8) << 8 | (g & 0xFC) << 3 | b >> 3

content.text:
Here's what I found on each. All the numbers for Rocks below are my arithmetic; none are measured.

## Reported problems

- **Triangle (rainbow):** this is my fault. The shim's `make_smooth_colormap` is our own. It always puts three anchors round the whole hue wheel at high saturation and brightness, so it's always a bright rainbow. Upstream picks 2–5 random colours, with random saturation (0–1) and brightness (0.2–1), rejects any pair too close together, and joins them in a loop. That gives the muted, earthy palettes. I'd rewrite ours to follow that behaviour without copying the code. It changes the colours of every hack that uses the smooth scheme, and the pinned hashes with them, so I need your go-ahead.
- **Penrose (screen full, no blank):** this is upstream behaviour, as you suspected. Its restart is a pause counted in frames: `COMPLETION` is 3141 frames, and `CELEBRATE` is 31415. `CELEBRATE` is used when the tiler hits an error or an untileable vertex. At 87 fps that's about 6 minutes, and about 5 minutes at X's usual rate. It also keeps growing into the square's corners, which the round screen hides. I'd shorten both pauses with a build-time patch, as I did for Celtic (the copy stays byte-identical). I'd aim for about 10 s, but that number is my call.
- **Lisa (speed varies):** the hack picks a random line width of 1–8 at each start. Width 1 takes the cheap line path and wider widths go through the polygon stroker. I measured 14.3 fps on one start, so that's one width, not the range. Options: speed up the stroker (shared code), or patch Lisa to cap the width. Capping is simplest, but it changes the look.

## Rocks and the shim

I need to correct my earlier note. The shim already has 1-bit bitmaps and `XCopyPlane` from them to the window. What it lacks is *drawing into* a bitmap: `XFillRectangle` and `XFillPolygon` do nothing there. Rocks fills a rock silhouette into about 400 bitmaps at start-up, then stamps them each frame. So the stamps are blank and only the tiny far dots, drawn as plain rectangles, show.

Adding bitmap fills is a real gap fill. I'd need to check it doesn't move any pinned hack (Goop creates a 1-bit pixmap), and the full suite would tell me. My estimates:

- **PSRAM:** about 2.7 MB of bitmaps, which fits beside the 7 MB free.
- **Start-up:** about 10 M pixel writes to fill the bitmaps, unless I fill them in spans with bit operations.
- **Frame rate:** the per-pixel `XCopyPlane` loop could limit it. I'd measure it before promising anything.

## DecayScreen image

The shim already has a blob format (`565M` in `ximage-loader.h`) and `tools/make_logo_blob.py`, which uses Pillow. So any PNG or JPEG is fine, and I'll convert it. Square, at least 466 px, with the subject centred (the screen is round) is ideal. Size matters because the image lives in flash. A full 466×466 blob is 434 KB, and I'd guess about 0.7 MB is left in the 3 MB partition, which I haven't checked. I'd store 320×320 (200 KB) and scale up, or 233×233 (108 KB) if space is tight. I'd wire it into `load_image_async_simple`, so any hack that wants a picture gets it. Rotzoomer and Twang are probably candidates, but I haven't checked.

## Questions for you

1. Shall I go ahead with the Triangle colours, the Penrose pause patch and the Rocks bitmap fills? The first and last change shared shim code.
2. For Lisa, should I cap the line width, or look at speeding up the stroker?
3. Which image, and is a 320 px stored size fine?

content.content:
"""PlatformIO pre-build script: with XS_LOGO=<image> set, writes a logo header
for Maze from that image; without it, removes any header left by an earlier
build so the committed logo is used.

maze_patched.c includes "images/gen/logo-50_png.h" from its own directory
first, so the generated copy wins without touching the include path. Relative
paths are taken from the repository root. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in
PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = (
    Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR"))  # noqa: F821
    / "generated"
    / "images"
    / "gen"
    / "logo-50_png.h"
)
LOGO_SIZE = 50

logo = os.environ.get("XS_LOGO")
if not logo:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    image = Path(logo)
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_LOGO={logo}: no such file ({image})")
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("XS_LOGO needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "logo_50_png",
            "--size",
            str(LOGO_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Maze logo: {image}")

def build_blob(width: int, height: int, rgba: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not (0 < width <= 0xFFFF and 0 < height <= 0xFFFF):
        raise ValueError(f"size {width}x{height} does not fit the blob header")
    if len(rgba) != width * height * 4:
        raise ValueError(f"expected {width * height * 4} RGBA bytes, got {len(rgba)}")

    pixels = bytearray()
    mask = bytearray()
    stride = (width + 7) // 8
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray(stride)
        for x in range(width):
            r, g, b, a = rgba[(y * width + x) * 4 :][:4]
            opaque = a >= OPAQUE_ALPHA
            pixels += (rgb565(r, g, b) if opaque else 0).to_bytes(2, "little")
            if opaque:
                row[x // 8] |= 0x80 >> (x % 8)
        mask += row
    header = b"565M" + width.to_bytes(2, "little") + height.to_bytes(2, "little")
    return bytes(header + pixels + mask)


def c_header(name: str, blob: bytes, source: str) -> str:
    guard = f"XSHIM_{name.upper()}_H"
    lines = []
    for i in range(0, len(blob), 12):
        lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blob[i : i + 12]) + ",")
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    return (
        f"/* Generated by tools/make_logo_blob.py from {source}; do not edit.\n"
        " * Despite the name (maze.c asks for a PNG), this is the raw blob\n"
        " * described in ximage-loader.h. */\n"
        f"#ifndef {guard}\n"
        f"#define {guard}\n"
        f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{\n"
        f"{body}\n"
        "};\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    from PIL import Image

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("image")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C array name")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--size",
        type=int,
        help="shrink to fit this many pixels square, keeping the aspect ratio "
        "(never enlarges)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    image = Image.open(args.image).convert("RGBA")
    if args.size:
        image.thumbnail((args.size, args.size), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    blob = build_blob(image.width, image.height, image.tobytes())

    # Left alone when unchanged, so an unchanged logo does not rebuild.
    output = Path(args.output)
    text = c_header(args.name, blob, Path(args.image).name)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not output.exists() or output.read_text() != text:
        output.write_text(text)
    print(f"{args.output}: {image.width}x{image.height}, {len(blob)} bytes")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

        mask += row
    header = b"565M" + width.to_bytes(2, "little") + height.to_bytes(2, "little")
    return bytes(header + pixels + mask)


def c_header(name: str, blob: bytes, source: str) -> str:
    guard = f"XSHIM_{name.upper()}_H"
    lines = []
    for i in range(0, len(blob), 12):
        lines.append("    " + ", ".join(f"0x{b:02x}" for b in blob[i : i + 12]) + ",")
    body = "\n".join(lines)
    return (
        f"/* Generated by tools/make_logo_blob.py from {source}; do not edit.\n"
        " * Despite the name (maze.c asks for a PNG), this is the raw blob\n"
        " * described in ximage-loader.h. */\n"
        f"#ifndef {guard}\n"
        f"#define {guard}\n"
        f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{\n"
        f"{body}\n"
        "};\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    from PIL import Image

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("image")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C array name")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--size",
        type=int,
        help="shrink to fit this many pixels square, keeping the aspect ratio "
        "(never enlarges)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    image = Image.open(args.image).convert("RGBA")
    if args.size:
        image.thumbnail((args.size, args.size), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    blob = build_blob(image.width, image.height, image.tobytes())

    # Left alone when unchanged, so an unchanged logo does not rebuild.
    output = Path(args.output)
    text = c_header(args.name, blob, Path(args.image).name)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not output.exists() or output.read_text() != text:
        output.write_text(text)
    print(f"{args.output}: {image.width}x{image.height}, {len(blob)} bytes")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Shrink maze.c's fixed-size arrays so it fits in the ESP32-S3's memory.

maze.c keeps its maze and three move lists in one `struct state` sized by
`MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X/Y` (1000 each), about 20 MB. The board has 8 MB of PSRAM. On
a 466 px screen with 7 px cells (the smallest the hack picks) a maze is 66
cells across, so 80 leaves room and the struct drops to about 130 KB.

The copied maze.c stays byte-identical to upstream. The firmware build writes
a patched copy with `firmware/patch_maze.py` and compiles that instead.
"""

import re

MAZE_LIMIT = 80
UPSTREAM_LIMIT = 1000


def patch_maze(source: str, limit: int) -> str:
    for axis in ("X", "Y"):
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"^#define[ \t]+MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis}[ \t]+{UPSTREAM_LIMIT}[ \t]*$",
            re.MULTILINE,
        )
        source, count = pattern.subn(f"#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis} {limit}", source)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"expected one `#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_{axis} {UPSTREAM_LIMIT}`, "
                f"found {count}; has upstream maze.c changed?"
            )
    return source
"""PlatformIO pre-build script: writes the patched maze.c that
src/hacks/maze_small.c includes. See tools/maze_patch.py for why."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
sys.path.insert(0, str(project.parent / "tools"))
import maze_patch

generated = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated"  # noqa: F821
generated.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

patched = maze_patch.patch_maze(
    (project / "src" / "hacks" / "maze" / "maze.c").read_text(),
    maze_patch.MAZE_LIMIT,
)
target = generated / "maze_patched.c"
if not target.exists() or target.read_text() != patched:
    target.write_text(patched)

env.Append(CPPPATH=[str(generated)])  # noqa: F821

import difflib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

import maze_patch as mp

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MAZE_C = ROOT / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "maze" / "maze.c"

SAMPLE = """#include <stdio.h>

#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X\t1000
#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_Y\t1000

#define MOVE_LIST_SIZE  (MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X * MAX_MAZE_SIZE_Y)
"""


def test_both_limits_are_replaced():
    out = mp.patch_maze(SAMPLE, 80)
    assert "#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X 80\n" in out
    assert "#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_Y 80\n" in out
    assert "1000" not in out


def test_nothing_else_changes():
    out = mp.patch_maze(SAMPLE, 80)
    changed = [
        line
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(
            SAMPLE.splitlines(), out.splitlines(), lineterm="", n=0
        )
        if line[0] in "+-" and line[:3] not in ("+++", "---")
    ]
    assert len(changed) == 4  # two lines out, two lines in


def test_missing_define_is_an_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="MAX_MAZE_SIZE_Y"):
        mp.patch_maze(SAMPLE.replace("#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_Y\t1000\n", ""), 80)


def test_unexpected_upstream_value_is_an_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X"):
        mp.patch_maze(SAMPLE.replace("X\t1000", "X\t2000"), 80)


def test_a_repeated_define_is_an_error():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X"):
        mp.patch_maze(SAMPLE + "#define MAX_MAZE_SIZE_X 1000\n", 80)


@pytest.mark.skipif(not MAZE_C.exists(), reason="maze.c not copied yet")
def test_real_maze_c_changes_exactly_two_lines():
    original = MAZE_C.read_text()
    out = mp.patch_maze(original, mp.MAZE_LIMIT)
    diff = [
        line
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(
            original.splitlines(), out.splitlines(), lineterm="", n=0
        )
        if line[0] in "+-" and line[:3] not in ("+++", "---")
    ]
    assert len(diff) == 4
    assert str(mp.MAZE_LIMIT) in out

 */

#define CELEBRATE 31415		/* This causes a pause, an error occurred. */
#define COMPLETION 3141		/* This causes a pause, tiles filled up screen. */

"""Shorten penrose.c's two pauses so a finished or failed tiling restarts soon.

penrose.c counts its pauses in frames, tuned for a fast X server:
`COMPLETION` (3141) after the tiles fill the screen and `CELEBRATE` (31415)
after an error it expects to recover from, which is about six minutes at the
board's 87 frames a second with the screen full and nothing moving. Both
become `PAUSE_FRAMES`, about ten seconds.

The copied penrose.c stays byte-identical to upstream. The firmware build
writes a patched copy with `firmware/patch_penrose.py` and compiles that.
"""

import re

PAUSE_FRAMES = 900
UPSTREAM = {"CELEBRATE": 31415, "COMPLETION": 3141}


def shorten_pauses(source: str, frames: int) -> str:
    for name, value in UPSTREAM.items():
        pattern = re.compile(
            rf"^#define[ \t]+{name}[ \t]+{value}\b[^\n]*$", re.MULTILINE
        )
        source, count = pattern.subn(f"#define {name} {frames}", source)
        if count != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"expected one `#define {name} {value}`, found {count}; "
                "has upstream penrose.c changed?"
            )
    return source

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The default is firmware/assets/grab-image.jpg, scaled to fit 320 pixels (about
217 KB of flash). XS_GRAB_IMAGE=<image> uses another (relative paths are taken
from the repository root) and XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none builds without one, so the
hacks that want a picture load nothing. A header from an earlier build is
removed in that case. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 320

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
if choice == "none":
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project / "assets" / "grab-image.jpg"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice}: no such file ({image})")
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

content.content:
# Display, canvas and runner gotchas

Moved verbatim from the Gotchas section of AGENTS.md.

- M5GFX reads a plain `uint32_t` colour as RGB888. `TFT_RED` and friends are
  RGB565 constants. The canvas holds pixels already byte-swapped into the
  display's order (`rgb565()` returns them that way), and the display runs
  with `setSwapBytes(false)`. A swap done by M5GFX on each push cost 10 ms of
  every frame (#23: pushes of 41-45 ms became 31 ms). `px_swap()` turns a
  canvas pixel into ordinary RGB565 and back: only code that reads colour bits
  needs it (the logo loader, `dump_main.c`, tests). A hue-sweeping palette
  stays a rainbow with its bytes swapped (red, green and blue rotate), so only
  pure black and white, or a colour you know (Maze's red flame, its green
  solving path), expose a wrong order on the device. Host frames cannot,
  since the swap happens in the push; compare them with `px_swap` applied.
- A hack that takes colour bits out of pixel values itself (Substrate's alpha
  blend, in `point2rgb`) breaks on swapped pixels without a compile error and
  without a crash. `substrate_single.c` swaps at `XAllocColor` and
  `XSetForeground` so the hack sees ordinary RGB565; its golden-frame test
  fails if either is missing. Searching for `XGetPixel` finds none of this:

  for it. It pulses every 16.82 ms for 1.1 ms. A full push is 20.6 ms copying
  into M5GFX's framebuffer plus 11.7 ms flushing to the panel (split by an
  outer `startWrite()` around the `pushImage`; the flush happens at the
  `endWrite`). `HackEntry::sync_to_refresh` (`XLOCKMORE_HACK_SYNCED`) starts
  the push `kTeSyncOffsetUs` after TE rises (`runner/te_sync.h`). Only
  Unknown Pleasures asks, because it costs up to a refresh of latency a frame.
- The offset (7.4 ms) is the middle of the clean window, found by a sweep:
  eight offsets across one refresh, 3 s each, the step number stamped on the
  screen, filmed at 120 fps. 3.2 to 9.5 ms had no vanished line in 39 updates;
  1.1 and 15.8 ms did, with the seam at film row 495 and film row 268: about 107
  film rows per millisecond (the camera frame is taller than the panel; the
  466-row panel scans about 28 rows per millisecond), so the bad window is only
  about 5 ms wide. It is valid for a full-frame push (the 20.6 ms copy). A push
  of another size moves the flush and the sweep would have to be repeated: the
  QR overlay's 328-row push is one, so a seam may show while the code is up.
  `-DTE_DIAG` logs the TE period and where pushes start.
- `te_sync.c` trusts few edges. Once it knows the period it accepts a rising
  edge only within period/16 of a whole number of periods since the last, so a
  missed edge or a stray pulse cannot move the lock; four misfits in a row drop
  the lock and relearn it. An edge further ahead than one period is stale (the
  32-bit microsecond counter can pass half its range with the line dead), and
  waiting stops 100 ms after the last edge. The ISR is placed in IRAM, but
  Arduino's pin dispatcher and `gpio_get_level` are in flash; that is safe only
  because `CONFIG_ARDUINO_ISR_IRAM` is unset. The run log's `sync=` is the wait
  for the edge and is left out of `push=`: compare `push=` across hacks, and add
  `sync=` to get the frame's latency.
- Reading a film of the display: iPhone slo-mo files store their first and
  last seconds at normal speed, so the label changes every ~100 frames there
  and every 360 in the 120 fps middle. Stabilise against the scenery (four
  corner patches; a mask edge around the display pins phase correlation at
  zero), level the rows, and count a vanish only when a line is missing across
  at least three 24 px windows on one row and not in a settled frame of the
  same update. A detector that finds nothing must also find the event you know
  is there: mine reported zero until a known vanish was used as a control, and
  reported many false events on steep line stretches until settled frames were.
- Every push also dims the screen: the dimmest band falls to 0.86 of its
  settled brightness for about 25 ms (three camera frames at 120 fps), at 5 Hz,
  with or without TE sync (0.860 synced, 0.870 unsynced). It is probably the
  "whole screen redraws" flicker. Its cause is not known. Rod sees no dimming
  with the sparser build (20 rows of 50 points, a step of about 91 ms against
  165), so it may track how much is lit or how long the copy runs; not yet
  filmed (issue #68).
- A hack's returned delay is waited after the push, and only the push counts
  against it, so its own step adds to the frame time: to hold a rate, return
  the target minus the step (`ad_flyingtoasters.c`: 19.5 fps became 28.9).

</system-reminder>

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The picture is vendor/grab-image.png when that exists, or the file named by
XS_GRAB_IMAGE (relative paths are taken from the repository root). It is
scaled to fit 466 pixels (a 640 by 480 screenshot becomes 466 by 350, about
340 KB of flash). Without either, or with XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none, nothing is
generated and a hack that wants a picture loads nothing. vendor/ is
git-ignored, so a picture someone else owns (the Windows 95 screenshot) stays
out of the repository. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in PlatformIO's
Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 466

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
image = None
if choice != "none":
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project.parent / "vendor" / "grab-image.png"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        if choice:
            sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice}: no such file ({image})")
        image = None

if image is None:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The default is firmware/assets/grab-image.jpg, scaled to fit 320 pixels (about
217 KB of flash). XS_GRAB_IMAGE=<image> uses another (relative paths are taken
from the repository root) and XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none builds without one, so the
hacks that want a picture load nothing. A header from an earlier build is
removed in that case. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 320

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
if choice == "none":
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project / "assets" / "grab-image.jpg"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice}: no such file ({image})")
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

new = """- Rocks and DecayScreen were wired, looked at and dropped in the 2026-10-12
  second batch, then brought back after Rod asked for the shim to be extended.
  Rocks stamps every rock bigger than 3 pixels with `XCopyPlane` from a
  depth-1 pixmap it filled with `XFillPolygon`, and the shim drew nothing into
  a bitmap, so only the far dots showed (a 3,000-frame dump looked nearly
  black): `XFillRectangle` and `XFillPolygon` now fill bitmaps. On the board it
  runs at 17.2 fps against its own 50 ms delay, and holds 2.66 MB of PSRAM and
  all but 32 KB of the internal heap while it runs (about 180 of its 400
  bitmaps are under the 4 KB internal limit); a rotation soak that left it for
  DecayScreen read heap and PSRAM back at their idle values. DecayScreen smears
  the picture `load_image_async_simple` paints (see `x11shim.md`); without one
  it stays black. Both were host-only findings from a frame dump: look at later
  frames (3,000) as well as 400 before pinning, and read what the hack draws
  with.
- Penrose (`penrose_short_pause.c`, `tools/penrose_patch.py`) restarts after
  900 frames (about 10 s at 87 fps) instead of 3,141 once the screen is full
  and 31,415 after an error it thinks it can recover from, about six minutes
  at the board's rate with nothing moving. Upstream counts those pauses in
  frames, tuned for a fast X server, so other devices show the same stall.
- Triangle's palette is `make_smooth_colormap`, which the shim now builds the
  way upstream picks it (two to five random colours, any saturation, never
  black): its first version was always a bright rainbow, and every hack that
  asks for a smooth map changed colour with the fix (24 pinned hashes moved,
  all looked at).
"""

open(p, "w").write(s)

s = open(p).read()

  is set where the GC's foreground is odd and cleared where it is even, and the
  clip mask and the GC's function are ignored. The polygon is even-odd, a pixel

content.text:
All twelve hacks are now in on `feature/batch5-s-m-hacks`. The branch is committed, with no push and no PR yet. The board is on the normal rotating build, flashed and hash-verified. The full host suite (714 tests), tools pytest (537 passed, 1 skipped), notices check and markdownlint all pass.

## Your fixes

- **Triangle (rainbow):** I rewrote `make_smooth_colormap` to pick 2–5 random colours the way upstream does. The host frame is now a brown-and-green landscape, which looks like the earth tones you expected. This changed the colours of 23 other hacks that use the smooth scheme, so I re-pinned their frame hashes. I looked at all 24 new frames first. None went flat or garbled, but they now look different, so some will want your eye.
- **Penrose (screen full, no blank):** the restart pauses were 3,141 frames after a full screen and 31,415 after an error, about six minutes at 87 fps. A build-time patch cuts both to 900 frames, about 10 s. The pause length is my pick. I checked the patch is applied in the built source but haven't watched it on the board.
- **Lisa (speed varies):** filed as #98 for stroker speed. I did not cap the width.
- **Rocks:** the shim now fills 1-bit bitmaps, so the rocks draw properly. On the board it runs at 17.2 fps, held back by its own 50 ms delay. It takes 2.66 MB of PSRAM and leaves only 32 KB of internal heap while it runs. A rotation soak showed heap and PSRAM fully back after it.
- **DecayScreen:** it now melts the Windows 95 screenshot at 65 fps. I made the shim scale and centre-crop the picture instead of stretching it, so the 4:3 screenshot loses its left and right edges. That cuts off the Start button, so you may want a different crop.

## The image

I didn't commit the screenshot. It's Microsoft's artwork, so I kept it in the git-ignored `vendor/grab-image.png`, as with the Flying Toasters art, and the build converts it. Without that file, DecayScreen stays black. Your headshot was never committed; I deleted my EXIF-stripped copy once you switched images. Say so if you do want the screenshot committed.

Flash is now 87.0% full, about 409 KB free, because the 466×350 picture costs 340 KB. A 320 px version would save about 150 KB if headroom matters.

## What I haven't verified

- **On-screen look:** colours and cropping are for you to judge.
- **Rotation soak:** not run across the whole registry.
- **Speed predictions:** the new hacks aren't in the speed-backtest holdout.

Next I'd push and open a draft PR with `entire trail create`, with those unverified items in the body. Shall I go ahead?

### The Maze logo

Maze draws the xscreensaver logo inside its maze. The logo data in
`logo-50_png.h` is `utils/images/logo-50.gif` from xscreensaver 6.16,
re-encoded as 50 by 50 RGB565 pixels and a transparency mask, without
changing the design. It is not part of the MIT-licensed code in this
repository.

The GIF has no licence text of its own. The C file that uses it,
`utils/logo.c`, credits the design to Angela Goodman, carries jwz's
permission notice (above) for its code, and asks that the logo not be
altered: "The logo is xscreensaver's identity". To use a different picture
in a local build without committing it, set `XS_LOGO` to the image file (see
`AGENTS.md`). The blob format is in `ximage-loader.h`.

### The Pacman sprites

Pacman draws its characters from `hacks/images/pacman.png` in xscreensaver
6.16, a 64 by 3840 sprite sheet. The file has no licence text of its own, and
this repository does not contain it. `firmware/pacman_sprites.py` reads it from
`vendor/` at build time and converts it to the raw blob described in
`ximage-loader.h` (3 MB as C text) in the build directory. The sprites are not
part of the MIT-licensed code in this repository.

### The XMatrix glyph sheets

XMatrix draws its characters from `hacks/images/matrix1.png`, `matrix1b.png`,
`matrix2.png` and `matrix2b.png` in xscreensaver 6.16, two sizes of two glyph

The screenshot is committed (`f1da11c`) with a notices section, and the pre-commit hooks passed. The tree is clean, nothing is pushed, and no PR is open. I made no change to the crop. I didn't reflash, because the board's firmware was built from identical image bytes (same 346,858-byte blob).

## Colours worth a second look

I judged these from one host frame each, so a device check of the palette is more reliable. The palette is also random on each start (the test needs at least 10% of starts muted and at least 10% dark, and the real rate is probably higher), so any single look can mislead. These are the ones I'd watch over a few rotations:

- **CWaves and Cynosure:** both looked washed-out in my frame, pale mauve bars and a dusty brown. That's within upstream's rules, but it's the weakest look I saw.
- **Thin lines on black, where a dark palette could make them hard to see:** Mountain, Critical, Euler2D, IFS, Rotor, Lissie, Spiral and Anemone. Hopalong also looked nearly empty, but that may just be its slow start.
- **Colour carries the meaning:** Celtic (strand colours), Halo and Moire2 (two-tone patterns), and BoxFit (the gradient across its circles).
- **Flame, Hexadrop, HexTrail, CloudLife, Discrete and Drift** also changed. They looked fine in my frame.

Roughly 30% of starts use a two-colour "there and back" palette, so a hack that looks two-tone is expected.

## Two things that went wrong during the commit

Neither lost any work.

- **Pre-commit cache:** it pointed at a hook-cache directory that no longer existed. I ran `pre-commit clean`, which only resets that cache, and the hooks re-fetched.
- **Worktree index:** git's index for this worktree then became corrupt. It had 91 of the 442 tracked files and 64 entries pointing at blobs that don't exist. `git fsck` showed history and every ref intact. I backed up the broken index file, removed it, rebuilt it from HEAD, and re-staged my four files. `git fsck` is clean now. I don't know what corrupted it. The suspects are the failed pre-commit runs or another process in the repo. If it recurs, check for another session using the checkout.

Next I'd push and open the draft PR with `entire trail create`, with the unverified items in the body. Shall I go ahead?

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The picture is firmware/assets/grab-image.png (a Windows 95 screenshot), or the
file named by XS_GRAB_IMAGE (relative paths are taken from the repository
root). It is scaled to fit 466 pixels (a 640 by 480 screenshot becomes 466 by
350, about 340 KB of flash). With XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none nothing is generated and
a hack that wants a picture loads nothing. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in
PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 466

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
image = None
if choice != "none":
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project / "assets" / "grab-image.png"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice or 'default'}: no such file ({image})")

if image is None:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

40	        [
41	            uv,
42	            "run",
43	            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
44	            str(image),
45	            "--name",
46	            "grab_image_blob",
47	            "--size",
48	            str(GRAB_SIZE),
49	            "-o",

ROOT = "/Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/.claude/worktrees/batch5-s-m-hacks"

# hacks.md: replace the "dropped" paragraph with what happened.
p = f"{ROOT}/.claude/rules/hacks.md"
s = open(p).read()
i = s.index("- Rocks and DecayScreen were wired, looked at and dropped")
j = s.index("- Abstractile holds about 6.1 MB")
new = """- Rocks and DecayScreen were wired, looked at and dropped in the 2026-10-12
  second batch, then brought back after Rod asked for the shim to be extended.
  Rocks stamps every rock bigger than 3 pixels with `XCopyPlane` from a
  depth-1 pixmap it filled with `XFillPolygon`, and the shim drew nothing into
  a bitmap, so only the far dots showed (a 3,000-frame dump looked nearly
  black): `XFillRectangle` and `XFillPolygon` now fill bitmaps. On the board it
  runs at 17.2 fps against its own 50 ms delay, and holds 2.66 MB of PSRAM and
  all but 32 KB of the internal heap while it runs (about 180 of its 400
  bitmaps are under the 4 KB internal limit); a rotation soak that left it for
  DecayScreen read heap and PSRAM back at their idle values. DecayScreen smears
  the picture `load_image_async_simple` paints (see `x11shim.md`); without one
  it stays black. Both were host-only findings from a frame dump: look at later
  frames (3,000) as well as 400 before pinning, and read what the hack draws
  with.
- Penrose (`penrose_short_pause.c`, `tools/penrose_patch.py`) restarts after
  900 frames (about 10 s at 87 fps) instead of 3,141 once the screen is full
  and 31,415 after an error it thinks it can recover from, about six minutes
  at the board's rate with nothing moving. Upstream counts those pauses in
  frames, tuned for a fast X server, so other devices show the same stall.
- Triangle's palette is `make_smooth_colormap`, which the shim now builds the
  way upstream picks it (two to five random colours, any saturation, never
  black): its first version was always a bright rainbow, and every hack that
  asks for a smooth map changed colour with the fix (24 pinned hashes moved,
  all looked at).
"""
s = s[:i] + new + s[j:]
open(p, "w").write(s)

# x11shim.md: bitmap fills, the grab image, the palette.
p = f"{ROOT}/.claude/rules/x11shim.md"
s = open(p).read()
s = s.rstrip("\n") + """
- `XFillRectangle` and `XFillPolygon` fill a depth-1 pixmap now (Rocks): a bit
  is set where the GC's foreground is odd and cleared where it is even, and the
  clip mask and the GC's function are ignored. The polygon is even-odd, a pixel
  being in when its centre is, in float. Other primitives still draw nothing on
  a bitmap. Halo, Moire2 and Goop keep their own planes or layers and did not
  move.
- `xshim_set_grab_image` (`grabclient.h`) gives `load_image_async_simple` a
  picture to paint over its target the next time a load starts: scaled to cover
  and cropped evenly at the sides (a 4:3 screenshot on the square screen loses
  its left and right edges), mask ignored, finishing at once as before. `main.cpp`
  sets it from the header `firmware/grab_image.py` writes into the build
  directory: `vendor/grab-image.png` if it exists (Rod's choice is the Windows
  95 screenshot from guidebookgallery.org, which is Microsoft's, so it stays in
  git-ignored `vendor/`), or `XS_GRAB_IMAGE=<file>`, and `XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none`
  builds without. It is stored at up to 466 pixels (a 466 by 350 blob is 340
  KB of flash: the build went from 2.39 MB to 2.74 MB, 87.0% of the app
  partition). The host tests set their own picture, so a pin never depends on
  the local file; `dump` sets it when the header exists. DecayScreen is
  unpinned for that reason (`test_decayscreen_melts_the_grab_image`). Boxfit's
  `grab` mode, off by default, would get the picture too.
- `make_smooth_colormap` follows upstream's behaviour (written from scratch, not
  copied): two to five random points in hue, saturation and value, repicked if
  adjacent ones are close or the average is too grey or dark, joined in a closed
  path with colours spaced by edge length. The first version always spanned the
  hue wheel at high saturation and value, so Triangle and 23 other pinned hacks
  were a bright rainbow.
"""
open(p, "w").write(s)

# assessment_measured.md.in
p = f"{ROOT}/tools/assessment_measured.md.in"
s = open(p).read()
old = "precision (`lisa_single.c`): 9.6 fps as copied, 14.3 after. Rocks and\nDecayScreen were tried and dropped (see `failed_ports.txt`).\n"
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, "precision (`lisa_single.c`): 9.6 fps as copied, 14.3 after. Rocks and\nDecayScreen were added in a second pass, once the shim filled bitmaps and\npainted a picture for a screen grab; Rocks holds 2.66 MB of PSRAM and leaves\nabout 32 KB of internal heap while it runs, and gives both back when it stops.\n", 1)
anchor = "| XRaySwarm | 22.8-23.0 | 21.2-21.6 ms | 0.9-2.8 ms | 19.4-21.6 ms | about 59 KB |\n"
assert anchor in s
s = s.replace(anchor, anchor + "| Rocks | 17.2-17.4 | 2.5-3.2 ms | 3.5-4.7 ms | 50.7-52.0 ms | about 2.66 MB |\n| DecayScreen | 63.6-66.8 | 3.3-3.9 ms | 4.3-5.0 ms | 6.7-7.3 ms | none measurable |\n", 1)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("ok")

import re

SP = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rod-build-stopwatch-screensaver/8efb68f3-5af6-4812-ab49-c8d5c605e5cb/scratchpad"
IDLE = 6989667


def rng(vals, unit, digits=1):
    lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
    f = f"{{:.{digits}f}}"
    if round(lo, digits) == round(hi, digits):
        return f.format(lo) + unit
    return f.format(lo) + "-" + f.format(hi) + unit


for h, label in {"rocks": "Rocks", "decayscreen": "DecayScreen"}.items():
    lines = [l for l in open(f"{SP}/{h}.log", errors="replace") if l.startswith("run ")][1:]
    rows = [dict(re.findall(r"(\w+)=([\d.]+)", l)) for l in lines]
    f = lambda k: [float(r[k]) for r in rows]
    extra = IDLE - min(f("psram"))
    extra_s = "none measurable" if extra < 10_000 else f"about {extra / 1e6:.2f} MB"
    print(f"| {label} | {rng(f('fps'), '')} | {rng(f('step'), ' ms')} | {rng(f('push'), ' ms')} | "
          f"{rng(f('wait'), ' ms')} | {extra_s} | heap {min(f('heap')):.0f}")

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/.claude/skills/markdown

# GitHub Flavored Markdown Generation

**Version:** 1.2.1

Generate GFM that passes markdownlint validation with zero violations.

## Core Principles

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

- Before/after ALL lists (MD032)
- Before/after ALL headings except document start (MD022)
- Before/after ALL code blocks (MD031)
- Between ALL block-level elements

### 2. Consistency Required

- Use `-` for lists
- Use `#` for headings (ATX)
- Regular spaces only—never tabs/nbsp

### 3. Structure Matters

- Heading hierarchy: 1→2→3 (not 1→3)
- ONE H1 per document
- Files end with one newline
- Lines under 80 chars

### 4. Invisible Characters Matter

- Use ONLY regular spaces (U+0020)
- Never non-breaking spaces (U+00A0,  )
- Never tabs
- UTF-8 encoding

## Pre-Generation Checklist

- [ ] Where will lists/headings/code appear?
- [ ] Heading levels verified (1→2→3)?
- [ ] Using `-` for all lists?
- [ ] Code languages specified?
- [ ] Lines under 80 chars?
- [ ] Line breaks needed? (two trailing spaces)
- [ ] Using regular spaces only?
- [ ] URLs wrapped in `<>` or `[]`?
- [ ] Document starts with H1?
- [ ] Ordered lists use `1.` for all items?
- [ ] File ends with single newline?
- [ ] Tables use consistent spacing?

## Essential Rules

### Lists (MD032, MD004)

```markdown
Text before.

- Item one
- Item two

Text after.
```

### Headings (MD001, MD022)

```markdown
Text.

## Heading

Content.
```

### Code Blocks (MD031, MD040)

````markdown
Text.

```python
code()
```

Text.
````

**Nested Fences:** When showing markdown examples that contain code blocks,
use **one more backtick** than the deepest level:

- Three backticks (` ``` `): Regular code
- Four backticks (` ```` `): Markdown examples with code
- Five backticks (` ````` `): Nested markdown examples

`````markdown
````markdown
# Example

```bash
command
```

````
`````

### Line Length (MD013)

Break long lines at natural points. Use reference-style links for long URLs.

### URLs and Email (MD034)

Wrap bare URLs and emails:

```markdown
Wrong: https://example.com
Right: <https://example.com>
Right: [link](https://example.com)

Wrong: user@example.com
Right: <user@example.com>
```

### Document Structure (MD041)

Start with H1 (or front matter then H1):

```markdown
# Document Title

First paragraph.
```

### Ordered Lists (MD029)

Use `1.` for all items:

```markdown
1. First
1. Second
1. Third
```

### File Endings (MD047)

End with single newline:

```text
Last content line.
[single newline]
[EOF]
```

### Table Column Style (MD060)

Use consistent spacing in tables. Three styles:

**Compact (recommended):** `| cell |` - single space around content

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Data | More data |
```

**Aligned:** Pipes vertically aligned with padding

**Tight:** `|cell|` - no spaces

Pick ONE style per document. Compact is preferred.

### Character Encoding

**Detection:** View → Render Whitespace in VS Code

**Fix:** Find `\u00A0` → Replace with space

**Critical for AI:** Two trailing spaces = intentional line breaks. Do NOT
remove them.

## Critical Error Patterns

### 1. List Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD032 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text:
- Item
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD032 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text:

- Item

Text.
```

### 2. Heading Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD022 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text.
## Head
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD022 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text.

## Head

Text.
```

### 3. Code Without Blanks/Language

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD031 MD040 -->

**Wrong:**

````markdown
Text:
```
code
```
Text.
````

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD031 MD040 -->

**Right:**

````markdown
Text:

```python
code
```

Text.
````

### 4. Inconsistent Markers

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
- Item
* Item
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD004 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
- Item
- Item
```

### 5. Skipping Levels

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
# Title

### Sub (skipped H2)
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
# Title

## Section

### Sub
```

## Post-Generation Validation

1. Lists have blank lines before/after
2. Headings have blank lines before/after
3. Code has blank lines before/after
4. Heading progression: 1→2→3→4
5. All lists use `-`
6. All code has language
7. Lines under 80 chars
8. Document starts with H1
9. URLs wrapped properly
10. Ordered lists use `1.`
11. File ends with one newline
12. Two trailing spaces used intentionally
13. Only regular spaces (no nbsp/tabs)
14. Tables use consistent column spacing

## Mental Model

Markdown is **blocks with mandatory spacing:**

```text
[Text Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Heading Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[List Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Code Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Text Block]
[EOF]
```

Every block transition = blank line required.

## Quick Patterns

**List:**

```markdown
text

- item

text
```

**Heading:**

```markdown
text

## Head

text
```

**Code:**

````markdown
text

```lang
code
```

text
````

**Nested:**

```markdown
- parent
  - child
- parent
```

**Ordered:**

```markdown
text

1. item
1. item

text
```

**Table:**

```markdown
text

| Header | Header |
| --- | --- |
| Cell | Cell |

text
```

## Common Languages

**Programming:** `python` `javascript` `java` `c` `cpp` `go` `rust` `ruby`
`php` `swift` `kotlin` `typescript`

**Shell:** `bash` `sh` `powershell` `cmd` `zsh`

**Markup:** `html` `css` `xml` `json` `yaml` `toml` `markdown`

**Database:** `sql` `postgresql` `mysql`

**Other:** `text` `diff` `log`

## Validation

```bash
markdownlint filename.md
```

Goal: Zero errors/warnings.

## Additional Resources

See bundled references:

- `references/complete-rules.md` - Full rule catalog
- `references/edge-cases.md` - Platform quirks
- `references/examples.md` - Detailed examples

## Remember

Most common: Missing blank lines around lists/headings/code.

**Two trailing spaces:** Intentional line breaks. Do NOT remove.

When in doubt:

1. Add blank lines before/after blocks
2. Use `-` for lists
3. Use `#` for headings
4. Specify code language
5. Increment headings by one
6. Use regular spaces only
7. Two trailing spaces = line break

# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Threads, GL, Xft, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |

colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |
